articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft drops 167 security fixes including a SharePoint zero-day and a Windows Defender flaw dubbed 'BlueHammer' — because apparently even the defenders need defending. Chrome also patched its fourth zero-day this year because 2026 is shaping up to be a banner year for bug hunting.

articles.title: Germany Doxes “UNKN,” Head of RU Ransomware Gangs REvil, GandCrab
articles.summary: Russian military intelligence weaponized ancient router vulnerabilities to mass-harvest Microsoft Office tokens like digital pickpockets at a tech conference. The campaign proves that sometimes the oldest tricks work best when everyone's too busy chasing shiny new threats.

articles.title: Digital Hopes, Real Power: From Connection to Collective Action
articles.summary: FOIA warriors used open records laws to expose ALPR surveillance abuse, so naturally states want to slam the transparency door shut. Because nothing says 'we're totally not doing anything sketchy' like making it illegal to see what you're doing.

articles.title: Open Records Laws Reveal ALPRs’ Sprawling Surveillance. Now States Want to Block What the Public Sees.
articles.summary: Utah's anti-VPN law goes live next week because apparently digital privacy is now a crime in the Beehive State. Expect VPN usage to spike faster than a teenager's heart rate when their parents walk in.

articles.title: OpenAI locks GPT-5.5-Cyber behind velvet rope despite slamming Anthropic for doing exactly that
articles.summary: Critical cPanel vulnerability already being exploited in the wild with ransomware following close behind. When the backbone of millions of websites gets pwned, everyone's day just got significantly worse.

articles.title: First reports come in of victims of critical cPanel vuln as 'millions' of sites potentially exposed
articles.summary: Britain's cyber agency warns that AI bug hunting is about to unleash a 'patch tsunami' as decades of buried code debt comes due all at once. The bill for years of 'we'll fix it later' shortcuts is finally arriving, and it's compound interest time.

articles.title: 30,000 Facebook Accounts Hacked via Google AppSheet Phishing Campaign
articles.summary: Cybersecurity company Trellix admits unauthorized access to its source code repository. Nothing quite screams confidence in your security products like getting your own crown jewels stolen.

articles.title: Polymarket Rejects Data Breach Claims as Hacker Alleges 300K Records Stolen
articles.summary: A 15-year-old allegedly hacked France's ID agency and tried to sell millions of citizen records on the dark web. Gen Z continues to prove that age is just a number when it comes to digital chaos.

articles.title: Anthropic Rolls Out Claude Security for AI Vulnerability Scanning
articles.summary: CopyFail Linux kernel vulnerability enables any user to escalate to root privileges across most distributions. Local privilege escalation vulnerabilities: because sometimes you don't need to break in when you can just walk upstairs.

articles.title: A Bridge to Somewhere: How to Link Your Mastodon, Bluesky, or Other Federated Accounts
articles.summary: Germany doxes 'UNKN,' the elusive mastermind behind REvil and GandCrab ransomware empires — 31-year-old Daniil Shchukin now has a face to match his legendary chaos. Another reminder that even the most shadowy digital ghosts eventually cast real-world shadows.
